anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the 6th signal pin of the servo header PWM_S1G2 is wired to NET0100, which is the Winbond NAND flash chip-select net (U19 pin 1 CS, also driven by FCC MCU pin PA4). The PCA9685 LED5 output (U7 pin 11) is NET0108, and NET0108 does not appear anywhere on the servo header. The header's 8 signal nets are {NET0022,NET0091,NET0173,NET0116,NET0144,NET0100,NET0047,NET0124} whereas the PCA9685 LED0-LED7 nets are {NET0022,NET0091,NET0173,NET0116,NET0144,NET0108,NET0047,NET0124} — i.e. LED5 (NET0108) is dropped from the header and flash CS (NET0100) is inserted in its place.
anomalies.expected: The 16-channel PWM driver's eight used outputs LED0-LED7 (U7 pins 6-13) must map one-to-one to the eight servo header signal pins, so header pin 6 should carry LED5 = NET0108. The SPI flash chip-select (NET0100) is a separate MCU-controlled signal and must not be merged with a servo PWM line.

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals sheet: PWM_S1G2 left column rows 1-8 = NET0022, NET0091, NET0173, NET0116, NET0144, NET0100, NET0047, NET0124
FCC Peripherals sheet: U7 PCA9685PW pin 11 LED5 = NET0108; U19 W25N01GVZEIG_TR pin 1 CS = NET0100

anomalies.impact: Servo header channel 6 is shorted to the SPI flash CS line: every MCU flash access pulses that header pin (a servo would twitch or be driven with non-PWM levels), and a servo connected there loads/disturbs the flash CS net, risking corrupted NAND reads/writes. Meanwhile the intended 6th PWM output (LED5/NET0108) is left unconnected, so that servo channel produces no signal.

The one drawing-supported deviation is on the FCC Peripherals sheet: servo header pin 6 is wired to the flash chip-select net NET0100 instead of the PCA9685 LED5 output NET0108, bridging the SPI flash CS line to a servo PWM header and leaving LED5 open.
